items.title: Mike Longo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2019
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Wow. Didn’t he do the thing with Thelonious Monk or something? [INTERVIEWEE] Yeah.

ctx.x: He thinks rhythm and puts notes to the rhythm. He told this lady in Florida, “Find yourself a rhythm and hang some notes on it.” So Dizzy, you know the tune “Champ”? [scats]. That’s the way he’s thinking. And he just put notes to the — now the notes, you might be looking up a scale, you might be looking up an arpeggio, you might be looking — but you’re playing the rhythms. And that’s the way Dizzy thought, and he also didn’t think trumpet, he thought piano. The first time Miles heard Dizzy and I play together he…

“ontological music.” What he meant by that was the music is out there, he more or less uncovers the music rather than composes it. It’s already out there. And Dizzy used to say the same thing in his way. He would say, “Man this music is just out here waiting for someone to come get it.” And he used to tell me, he’d say “If the music tells you, you go where the music is.”
